## 1. Spec

Turn the intent into `spec.md`, the design an engineer builds from. No
code. Start from how the system works today (`docs/architecture.md` and the
code) and describe the change against it: the new and changed rules; the
API changes, with request and response examples and every new error; how
the server enforces the rules without keeping state; the page (what shows
when, keyboard and screen-reader use, small screens); which modules change
and how; what must keep working exactly as before; and how each line of the
intent's "How we will know it worked" and "What must not change" will be
checked. End with **Open questions**: each one gets the decision you took,
so nothing blocks the next phase.

## 2. Plan

Turn `spec.md` into `plan.md`, an implementation plan. No code. The first
line is `# Plan: <title>`. Then 2 to 4 phases, each a heading
`## Phase N: <name>` followed only by task lines `- [ ] <task>`, 3 to 6
tasks each. Each phase ends with a task that verifies it by running
something, and leaves the game working. Verification uses what every
session has: `python3` (the tests, a throwaway script, a server started
with `--port 0` and driven with `urllib`) and `ruff`. No browser and no
other tools: how the page looks and feels is checked by a person at the
preview after phase 3, so list those checks under a final heading
`## For the preview` as plain bullets, not boxes. Writing new tests is
phase 4 of this process, not part of this plan, but the existing tests
must keep passing after every phase.

## 3. Implement

Implement the first phase of `plan.md` that still has unchecked boxes, and
only that phase. Tick each box (`- [ ]` to `- [x]`) as soon as its task is
done, one edit per task. Follow `spec.md`. If you must depart from it,
update `spec.md` so the two agree. Keep `docs/architecture.md` true. Do not
write new tests yet, but run the existing ones. If a verify task asks for
something you cannot run, do the part you can, tick it, and add what is
left to `## For the preview`.

## Preview (done by a person)

A person runs the change on a preview server, goes through
`## For the preview`, and records the result in `preview.md`: who, when,
and what passed or failed. That file is the sign-off for everything only a
browser can show. Later phases read it; they do not repeat those checks.

## 4. Unit tests

Write pytest tests in `tests/` for every rule in `spec.md`, next to the
existing ones: every new rule, every new error, and every "must not change"
promise of the intent. Call the code directly, not over the network. Run
the whole suite. If a test finds a bug, fix the code and say so in your
final message.

## 5. System test

Test the real system from the outside, extending `tests/system/`: start
`python3 -m tictactoe --port 0` as a process and, over HTTP, play the new
feature end to end, including the attempts the intent says must fail, and
show that the old game still behaves as before. Always stop the server,
even when a test fails. Run the whole suite. Write `test-report.md`: what
was tested, the result, and any bugs found and fixed.

## 6. Lint

Run `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`. Fix every finding in the
code, run the tests again, and stop when both are clean and the tests pass.
Never silence a finding (see `CLAUDE.md`).

the diff of the change (`git diff` against the commit before its spec) and

code. Write `review.md`: one line per finding,

```markdown
- [ ] **blocker|major|minor** `path:line`: what is wrong, and why it matters
```

most severe first, then a one-paragraph verdict. If there is nothing to
report at some severity, say so; do not invent findings.

are cheap. Tick each finding as you fix it. Leave a finding you decide not
to fix unticked, with the reason after it. Add a test for every bug you
fix. Finish with the tests and lint clean.

Follow `docs/deploy.md`.

# Intent: a secret cheat code

*From: Product. For: the games team. Change name: `cheat-code`.*

## Why

Tic-tac-toe has been live for a month. People play, but Hard can never be
beaten, and many players quit after two or three draws. Players love
secrets they can share with friends: we want a hidden cheat code that lets
you beat the computer once in a while. Players will pass the code around,
which brings them back to the page and brings their friends.

## What we want

- A secret code typed on the keyboard during a game against the computer
  unlocks a cheat for that game: the player may **steal** one square from
  the computer. The computer's mark on that square becomes the player's
  mark, and that counts as the player's move.
- One steal per game. It is never shown or hinted at on the page until the
  code has been typed. After that, the page makes clear how to use it.
- The code is the classic one: up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right,
  B, A.
- A game won with a steal is announced differently ("You won... with a
  little help"), and it is counted separately in the score. It must not
  count as a normal win.
- The cheat works only against the computer, at both levels, and not when
  two friends play on the same screen.

## What must not change

- Without the code, the game behaves exactly as it does today, and Hard
  still never loses to fair play.
- On the page, nobody can steal without typing the code. Nobody can steal
  twice in a game, even by sending requests to the server by hand.

## How we will know it worked

- It is live in production, the old game unchanged.
- People share the code: we see steals in games we did not set up ourselves.

Source: `changes/cheat-code/intent.md`. This is the design to build from.

## Summary

Against the computer, typing ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A on the page unlocks a
**steal** for the current game: once per game the player may turn one of
the computer's O squares into an X, and that is the player's move. A win
that used a steal is announced as "You won... with a little help" and
counted in its own score column, never as a normal win.

The browser recognises the code and shows the steal controls. The server
judges every steal. To enforce "one steal per game" without keeping state,
the server signs each game position it hands out (an HMAC **game token**)
and accepts a steal only together with a valid token that says no steal has
been used. Requests without a token behave exactly as today.

  accepts a board only if X count − O count is 0 or 1.

## New and changed rules

1. **Steal.** In a game against the computer, on the player's turn (X to
   move, game still playing), the player may name one cell that holds `"O"`.

   replies as usual if the game goes on.
2. **Once per game.** A game has at most one steal. A game is one unbroken
   chain of positions handed out by the server, starting from the empty
   board (see "Game token").
3. **Only against the computer**, at both levels (`easy`, `hard`). Never in
   `friend` mode.
4. **Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so the
   counts no longer say whose turn it is. The rule becomes: with `s` steals
   used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `s`,
   otherwise O. A valid board has X count − O count equal to `s` or `s + 1`.

5. **A steal can win at once.** If the stolen square completes a line of X,
   the game is won by X and the computer does not move. A steal never fills
   an empty square, so it cannot cause a draw by itself.
6. **Assisted win.** A game won by X in which a steal was used is an
   *assisted* win. The server says so in every answer (`assisted: true`).

   only in the "With help" column, not in "X wins".
7. After a steal the game goes on normally: the computer (either level)
   plays its best/random move from the new position, and the computer can
   still win or draw. Those are counted as today (O win, draw).
8. **The code.** ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A (`ArrowUp ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowDown

trust when the browser sends it back, as `CLAUDE.md` allows.

  never logged, never sent, never put in an error message.

  written as `X`, `O` or `-`. Example: `"0.3f9a…c1"` (64 hex digits).
  The token binds the board, the level and the steal count together;
  change any of them and it no longer verifies.

  string, has the wrong shape, an `<s>` other than `0`/`1`, or a MAC that

Each phase is done by a fresh session that reads the artifacts of the
earlier phases and leaves its own for the next one. The files are the only
memory, so write each artifact for a reader who was not there. Below,
`<change>` stands for `changes/<name>/`.

| # | Phase | Reads | Leaves |
|---|-------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Spec | `<change>/intent.md`, the code, `docs/` | `<change>/spec.md` |
| 2 | Plan | `<change>/spec.md`, the code | `<change>/plan.md` |
| 3 | Implement | `<change>/plan.md`, `<change>/spec.md` | code, `docs/architecture.md` |
| - | Preview (a person) | `## For the preview` in `plan.md` | `<change>/preview.md` |
| 4 | Unit tests | `<change>/spec.md`, the code | `tests/` |
| 5 | System test | `<change>/spec.md`, the code | `tests/system/`, `<change>/test-report.md` |
| 6 | Lint | the code | clean ruff |
| 7 | Code review | everything | `<change>/review.md` |
| 8 | Review fixes | `<change>/review.md` | fixes, ticked `review.md` |
| 9 | Deploy | `docs/deploy.md` | a release in production |

## 1. Spec

Turn the intent into `spec.md`, the design an engineer builds from. No
code. Start from how the system works today (`docs/architecture.md` and the
code) and describe the change against it: the new and changed rules; the
API changes, with request and response examples and every new error; how
the server enforces the rules without keeping state; the page (what shows
when, keyboard and screen-reader use, small screens); which modules change
and how; what must keep working exactly as before; and how each line of the
intent's "How we will know it worked" and "What must not change" will be
checked. End with **Open questions**: each one gets the decision you took,
so nothing blocks the next phase.

## 2. Plan

Turn `spec.md` into `plan.md`, an implementation plan. No code. The first
line is `# Plan: <title>`. Then 2 to 4 phases, each a heading
`## Phase N: <name>` followed only by task lines `- [ ] <task>`, 3 to 6
tasks each. Each phase ends with a task that verifies it by running
something, and leaves the game working. Verification uses what every
session has: `python3` (the tests, a throwaway script, a server started
with `--port 0` and driven with `urllib`) and `ruff`. No browser and no
other tools: how the page looks and feels is checked by a person at the
preview after phase 3, so list those checks under a final heading
`## For the preview` as plain bullets, not boxes. Writing new tests is
phase 4 of this process, not part of this plan, but the existing tests
must keep passing after every phase.

## 3. Implement

Implement the first phase of `plan.md` that still has unchecked boxes, and
only that phase. Tick each box (`- [ ]` to `- [x]`) as soon as its task is
done, one edit per task. Follow `spec.md`. If you must depart from it,
update `spec.md` so the two agree. Keep `docs/architecture.md` true. Do not
write new tests yet, but run the existing ones. If a verify task asks for
something you cannot run, do the part you can, tick it, and add what is
left to `## For the preview`.

## Preview (done by a person)

A person runs the change on a preview server, goes through
`## For the preview`, and records the result in `preview.md`: who, when,
and what passed or failed. That file is the sign-off for everything only a
browser can show. Later phases read it; they do not repeat those checks.

## 4. Unit tests

Write pytest tests in `tests/` for every rule in `spec.md`, next to the
existing ones: every new rule, every new error, and every "must not change"
promise of the intent. Call the code directly, not over the network. Run
the whole suite. If a test finds a bug, fix the code and say so in your
final message.

## 5. System test

Test the real system from the outside, extending `tests/system/`: start
`python3 -m tictactoe --port 0` as a process and, over HTTP, play the new
feature end to end, including the attempts the intent says must fail, and
show that the old game still behaves as before. Always stop the server,
even when a test fails. Run the whole suite. Write `test-report.md`: what
was tested, the result, and any bugs found and fixed.

## 6. Lint

Run `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`. Fix every finding in the
code, run the tests again, and stop when both are clean and the tests pass.
Never silence a finding (see `CLAUDE.md`).

## 7. Code review

Act as a reviewer who did not write this change. Read the intent, the spec,
the diff of the change (`git diff` against the commit before its spec) and
the code around it. Look for: bugs; gaps between intent, spec, code and
`docs/architecture.md`; rules that are not tested; security (the server
faces the internet and trusts no request); and accessibility. The browser
checks belong to `preview.md`: a problem it reports is a finding, but how
much a sign-off is worth (who looked, how closely) is for whoever releases
to judge, so say it in the verdict, not as a finding. Do not change any
code. Write `review.md`: one line per finding,

```markdown
- [ ] **blocker|major|minor** `path:line`: what is wrong, and why it matters
```

most severe first, then a one-paragraph verdict. If there is nothing to
report at some severity, say so; do not invent findings.

## 8. Review fixes

Fix every blocker and major finding in `review.md`, and the minors that
are cheap. Tick each finding as you fix it. Leave a finding you decide not
to fix unticked, with the reason after it. Add a test for every bug you
fix. Finish with the tests and lint clean.

## 9. Deploy

Follow `docs/deploy.md`.

# Intent: a secret cheat code

*From: Product. For: the games team. Change name: `cheat-code`.*

## Why

Tic-tac-toe has been live for a month. People play, but Hard can never be
beaten, and many players quit after two or three draws. Players love
secrets they can share with friends: we want a hidden cheat code that lets
you beat the computer once in a while. Players will pass the code around,
which brings them back to the page and brings their friends.

## What we want

- A secret code typed on the keyboard during a game against the computer
  unlocks a cheat for that game: the player may **steal** one square from
  the computer. The computer's mark on that square becomes the player's
  mark, and that counts as the player's move.
- One steal per game. It is never shown or hinted at on the page until the
  code has been typed. After that, the page makes clear how to use it.
- The code is the classic one: up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right,
  B, A.
- A game won with a steal is announced differently ("You won... with a
  little help"), and it is counted separately in the score. It must not
  count as a normal win.
- The cheat works only against the computer, at both levels, and not when
  two friends play on the same screen.

## What must not change

- Without the code, the game behaves exactly as it does today, and Hard
  still never loses to fair play.
- On the page, nobody can steal without typing the code. Nobody can steal
  twice in a game, even by sending requests to the server by hand.

## How we will know it worked

- It is live in production, the old game unchanged.
- People share the code: we see steals in games we did not set up ourselves.

1	# Spec: a secret cheat code (`cheat-code`)
2	
3	Source: `changes/cheat-code/intent.md`. This is the design to build from.
4	It describes the change against the system as it is today
5	(`docs/architecture.md`, `tictactoe/`).
6	
7	## Summary
8	
9	Against the computer, typing ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A on the page unlocks a
10	**steal** for the current game: once per game the player may turn one of
11	the computer's O squares into an X, and that is the player's move. A win
12	that used a steal is announced as "You won... with a little help" and
13	counted in its own score column, never as a normal win.
14	
15	The browser recognises the code and shows the steal controls. The server
16	judges every steal. To enforce "one steal per game" without keeping state,
17	the server signs each game position it hands out (an HMAC **game token**)
18	and accepts a steal only together with a valid token that says no steal has
19	been used. Requests without a token behave exactly as today.
20	
21	## How it works today (the parts this change touches)
22	
23	- A board is 9 cells, `"X"`, `"O"` or `""`. Whose turn it is follows from
24	  the counts: `game.turn()` is X when X count == O count. `game.validate()`
25	  accepts a board only if X count − O count is 0 or 1.
26	- `POST /api/move` takes the whole board, `cell`, `mode`, `level`. Against
27	  the computer the player is X and the board must have X to move. The server
28	  plays `cell`, then the computer's reply, and answers the new board.
29	- The server trusts nothing: any board that passes `validate()` is accepted.
30	  It has no idea whether that board came from a real game.
31	- The score (X wins, O wins, draws) lives in `app.js` until reload.
32	
33	## New and changed rules
34	
35	1. **Steal.** In a game against the computer, on the player's turn (X to
36	   move, game still playing), the player may name one cell that holds `"O"`.
37	   That cell becomes `"X"`. This is the player's move: the computer then
38	   replies as usual if the game goes on.
39	2. **Once per game.** A game has at most one steal. A game is one unbroken
40	   chain of positions handed out by the server, starting from the empty
41	   board (see "Game token").
42	3. **Only against the computer**, at both levels (`easy`, `hard`). Never in
43	   `friend` mode.
44	4. **Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so the
45	   counts no longer say whose turn it is. The rule becomes: with `s` steals
46	   used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `s`,
47	   otherwise O. A valid board has X count − O count equal to `s` or `s + 1`.
48	   With `s = 0` both rules are exactly today's.
49	5. **A steal can win at once.** If the stolen square completes a line of X,
50	   the game is won by X and the computer does not move. A steal never fills
51	   an empty square, so it cannot cause a draw by itself.
52	6. **Assisted win.** A game won by X in which a steal was used is an
53	   *assisted* win. The server says so in every answer (`assisted: true`).
54	   The page announces it as "You won... with a little help" and counts it
55	   only in the "With help" column, not in "X wins".
56	7. After a steal the game goes on normally: the computer (either level)
57	   plays its best/random move from the new position, and the computer can
58	   still win or draw. Those are counted as today (O win, draw).
59	8. **The code.** ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A (`ArrowUp ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowDown
60	   ArrowLeft ArrowRight ArrowLeft ArrowRight b a`, B and A in either case).
61	   The code is recognised by the page only; it unlocks the steal controls
62	   for the current game. The server does not check the code (see Open
63	   questions 1).
64	
65	## Game token (how the server enforces the rules without state)
66	
67	The server keeps nothing between requests. Instead it signs what it must
68	trust when the browser sends it back, as `CLAUDE.md` allows.
69	
70	- **Key.** `TICTACTOE_SECRET` from the environment (UTF-8 bytes) when set
71	  and not empty; otherwise 32 random bytes from `secrets.token_bytes` made
72	  once when the process starts. Production sets it through `ops/deploy.sh`
73	  and keeps it across releases, so tokens survive a deploy. The key is
74	  never logged, never sent, never put in an error message.
75	- **Format.** `"<s>.<mac>"`, where `<s>` is the number of steals used (`0`
76	  or `1`) and `<mac>` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the message
77	  `tictactoe-game-v1|<level>|<s>|<cells>`, with `<cells>` the 9 cells, each
78	  written as `X`, `O` or `-`. Example: `"0.3f9a…c1"` (64 hex digits).
79	  The token binds the board, the level and the steal count together;
80	  change any of them and it no longer verifies.
81	- **Checking.** Compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. A token that is not a
82	  string, has the wrong shape, an `<s>` other than `0`/`1`, or a MAC that
83	  does not match the request's `board` and `level` is rejected with
84	  `400 {"error": "the game token does not match this game"}`. This applies
85	  to any request that carries a `game` field, steal or not.
86	- **When the server hands one out** (the `game` field of the answer), only
87	  in `computer` mode and only while the game is still `playing`:
88	  - the request carried a valid token: the new position gets a token with
89	    the same `s` (or `s = 1` if this request was the steal);
90	  - the request had no token and its board was empty (first move of a new
91	    game): the new position gets a token with `s = 0`;
92	  - otherwise (no token, board not empty, e.g. a hand-made mid-game board
93	    or an older page): `game` is `null`. That game plays exactly as today
94	    and can never steal.
95	  So a token proves that the position was reached by legal moves through
96	  this server from an empty board, with `s` steals on the way.
97	- **Why this stops a second steal, even by hand.** A steal needs a token
98	  with `s = 0`. The answer to a steal only ever carries `s = 1` tokens, and
99	  every later answer in that game keeps `s = 1`. A board that has had a
100	  steal has X − O == 1 on X's turn, which no `s = 0` token can match and
101	  which `validate()` rejects without a token. Forging an `s = 0` token
102	  needs the key.
103	- **Replays.** Because the server is stateless, an old token stays valid.
104	  A player who kept an `s = 0` token from earlier in the same game can go
105	  back to that position and steal from there. That is a branch of the game
106	  (like an undo), and every branch still has at most one steal. Accepted
107	  (Open questions 3).
108	
109	## API changes
110	
111	`POST /api/move` keeps its path, limits (1024-byte body, 411, 413, 404,
112	405) and every existing field and error. New, all optional in the request:
113	
114	| Field | Meaning |
115	|-------|---------|
116	| `steal` | A cell 0–8 to steal, sent **instead of** `cell`. |
117	| `game` | The `game` token from the server's previous answer. |
118	
119	New in every `200` answer (all modes):
120	
121	| Field | Meaning |
122	|-------|---------|
123	| `game` | Token for the new position, or `null` (rules above). |
124	| `stealable` | Cells the player could steal now: the O cells when this answer has a token with `s = 0`, the game is playing and X is to move; otherwise `[]`. |
125	| `steal_used` | `true` once a steal has been used in this game (`s = 1`), else `false`. |
126	| `assisted` | `true` when `status` is `won`, `winner` is `X` and `steal_used` is `true`; else `false`. |
127	
128	The page uses `stealable`, `steal_used` and `assisted` as given; it never
129	works out for itself which squares can be stolen or whether a win was
130	assisted.
131	
132	### Examples (Hard; tokens shortened)
133	
134	First move of a new game, no token (the existing request, unchanged):
135	
136	```json
137	{"board": ["", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 0, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard"}
138	```
139	
140	```json
141	{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "status": "playing",
142	 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 4,
143	 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [4], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
144	```
145	
146	Next move, sending the token back:
147	
148	```json
149	{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 8, "mode": "computer",
150	 "level": "hard", "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
151	```
152	
153	```json
154	{"board": ["X", "O", "", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"], "status": "playing",
155	 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 1,
156	 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [1, 4], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
157	```
158	
159	The steal: taking the centre completes the diagonal 0-4-8.
160	
161	```json
162	{"board": ["X", "O", "", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"], "steal": 4, "mode": "computer",
163	 "level": "hard", "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
164	```
165	
166	```json
167	{"board": ["X", "O", "", "", "X", "", "", "", "X"], "status": "won",
168	 "winner": "X", "line": [0, 4, 8], "turn": null, "computer_move": null,
169	 "game": null, "stealable": [], "steal_used": true, "assisted": true}
170	```
171	
172	A steal that does not win (stealing cell 1 instead) gets the computer's
173	reply and an `s = 1` token; X is to move with X − O == 1. (Hard must block
174	row 0 at cell 2; this reply is the expected one, not recorded from code.)
175	
176	```json
177	{"board": ["X", "X", "O", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"], "status": "playing",
178	 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 2,
179	 "game": "1.<64 hex>", "stealable": [], "steal_used": true, "assisted": false}
180	```
181	
182	A friend game answers `game: null, stealable: [], steal_used: false,
183	assisted: false` in addition to today's fields.
184	
185	### New errors (all `400 {"error": "..."}`)
186	
187	Checked in this order, after today's checks of the body, `board` shape,
188	`mode` and `level`:
189	
190	| Case | Message |
191	|------|---------|
192	| `game` present but not valid for this `board` and `level` (any request) | `the game token does not match this game` |
193	| both `cell` and `steal` present | `send either cell or steal, not both` |
194	| `steal` in `friend` mode | `you can only steal from the computer` |
195	| `steal` without `game` | `a steal needs the game token from the last answer` |
196	| `steal` with a token whose `s` is 1 | `you have already stolen a square in this game` |
197	| `steal` not a whole number 0–8 (`true` is not a number) | `steal must be a whole number from 0 to 8` |
198	| game already over | `the game is over` (today's message) |
199	| the cell is not an O (empty or X) | `you can only steal one of the computer's squares` |
200	
201	The board check uses the token's `s`: a board with X − O outside
202	`s`..`s + 1` is rejected with today's message `X moves first and the
203	players alternate`, and with X − O ≠ `s` against the computer with today's
204	`against the computer you play X`.
205	
206	## Logging (to see steals in production)
207	
208	The intent will judge success by steals in games "we did not set up". The
209	server has no database, so after every successful steal the request handler
210	writes one line through `log_message` (stderr, which `ops/deploy.sh` sends
211	to `production/server.log`, next to the request line with the client
212	address):
213	
214	```text
215	steal level=hard cell=4 status=won assisted=true
216	```
217	
218	Nothing else is logged: no token, no key, no board. Because a steal needs a
219	token chain that started from an empty board, every logged steal happened
220	in a real game played through the server.
221	
222	## The page
223	
224	### Before the code (unchanged)
225	
226	The page looks and behaves exactly as today: no steal button, no hint, no
227	"With help" column, no change to labels or status texts. The new elements
228	exist in `index.html` with `hidden` and are not shown or announced.
229	
230	### Recognising the code
231	
232	- `app.js` listens to `keydown` on `document` and keeps the last 10 keys.
233	  When they equal the code, the code is typed. A sliding window means extra
234	  keys before it do not matter (↑ ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ … still works).
235	- Ignored: events with Ctrl, Alt or Meta held, and auto-repeat
236	  (`event.repeat`). Keys typed while focus is in a `<select>` are not
237	  recorded (arrows there change the mode or level, which starts a new game).
238	- The board's own arrow handling stays as it is: typing the code with the
239	  focus on the board moves the focus around, which is harmless; arrows never
240	  play a move.
241	- The code unlocks only when the mode is `computer` and the game is
242	  `playing`. Otherwise it does nothing at all (friend mode: no message, no
243	  hint).
244	- Unlocking lasts for the current game. A new game (button, mode or level
245	  change) locks it again; typing the code again unlocks it again.
246	
247	### After the code
248	
249	- The status line (`aria-live`) announces: "Cheat unlocked! Once this game,
250	  you may steal one of the computer's squares." The current status text
251	  follows after the next move as usual.
252	- A panel under the status line appears with a **Steal a square** button
253	  (`aria-pressed`) and the short text "Press Steal, then choose an O. Esc
254	  cancels." The button is disabled-looking (`aria-disabled="true"`, still
255	  focusable) when `stealable` is empty, with the reason in the panel text:
256	  "No O to steal yet" before the computer has moved, "Steal used" after.
257	- The score table shows a fourth column **With help** (and keeps showing it
258	  until the page is reloaded, so the count stays visible).
259	
260	### Steal mode
261	
262	- Pressing the button (click, Enter, Space) turns steal mode on, but only
263	  if `stealable` is not empty. The status line says "Steal: choose one of
264	  the computer's squares." The focus moves to the lowest stealable square
265	  (roving `tabindex` as today).
266	- In steal mode only the squares in `stealable` are active
267	  (`aria-disabled="false"`, class `stealable` with a visible dashed outline
268	  that does not rely on colour alone). Their label gains ", can be stolen",
269	  e.g. "Row 2, column 2, O, can be stolen". Every other square is
270	  `aria-disabled="true"` and does nothing when chosen.
271	- Choosing a stealable square (click, tap, Enter, Space) sends
272	  `{board, steal, mode, level, game}`. Steal mode ends with the answer.
273	- Esc, or pressing the button again, ends steal mode without a move and
274	  puts the focus back on the button.
275	- Outside steal mode, clicking an O does nothing, as today.
276	
277	### After a steal
278	
279	- The status line says "You stole row R, column C." when the game goes on
280	  (then the usual "Your turn (X)" once the next answer arrives; moving the
281	  focus with the arrow keys keeps the message), and "You won... with
282	  a little help" when the steal or a later move wins with `assisted: true`.
283	- Score: `assisted: true` adds 1 to **With help** and nothing to X wins.
284	  A computer win or a draw after a steal counts as today.
285	- The panel says "Steal used" and the button stays disabled-looking.
286	
287	### Small screens
288	
289	The panel and the four-column score table must fit 320 px wide with no
290	horizontal scroll: the column headings are short ("X wins", "O wins",
291	"Draws", "With help") and the button is at least 44 px tall. The code
292	needs a keyboard, so phones without one cannot unlock it (Open questions 2).
293	
294	## Modules
295	
296	| File | Change |
297	|------|--------|
298	| `game.py` | `turn(board, steals=0)`, `validate(board, steals=0)`, `play(board, cell, steals=0)` follow rule 4. New `steal(board, cell, steals) -> list[str]`: checks and errors from the table above (already stolen, cell type, game over, not X's turn, not an O); returns a new board, never changes its input. New `check_cells(board)`: only the shape and cell checks of `validate` (which now calls it), so the server can check a board's shape before it knows the token's `s`. `outcome()` and `legal_moves()` do not change. |
299	| `ai.py` | `choose_move(board, level, rng=None, *, steals=0)`; `best_move` and `value` take `steals` too (still cached), so the search uses the right turn after a steal. With `steals=0` the moves are exactly today's. |
300	| new `signing.py` | The key (env or random at import, as above), `sign(board, level, steals) -> str`, `verify(token, board, level) -> int` (returns `s`, raises `IllegalMoveError`). Nothing else imports `os.environ`. |
301	| `server.py` | `handle_move` reads `game` and `steal`, verifies, plays the move or the steal, then the computer's reply with the right `steals`, and adds `game`, `stealable`, `steal_used`, `assisted`. `describe()` takes `steals`. `do_POST` writes the steal log line. Signature `handle_move(request)` stays. |
302	| `static/index.html` | Hidden cheat panel (button + text) under the status line; hidden "With help" column in the score table. |
303	| `static/app.js` | Code recognition, unlock state per game, steal mode, sending `game` back with every move, the new status texts, the fourth score counter. |
304	| `static/style.css` | `.stealable` outline, panel layout, small-screen fit. |
305	| `docs/architecture.md` | Updated in phase 3: the token, the new fields and errors, the turn rule, `signing.py`, the page's cheat. |
306	
307	## What must keep working exactly as before
308	
309	- Every request without `steal` and without `game` gets the same `board`,
310	  `status`, `winner`, `line`, `turn`, `computer_move` and the same errors
311	  as today; the only difference is the four added fields.
312	- Hard is unchanged for `steals=0` and never loses to fair play
313	  (`test_hard_never_loses` passes untouched). Easy is unchanged.
314	- Friend mode, `/health` (`200 ok`), the assets, 404/405/411/413, the
315	  1024-byte limit, the keyboard model of the board and its labels.
316	- All existing tests pass without change.
317	
318	## How each line of the intent will be checked
319	
320	| Intent line | Check |
321	|-------------|-------|
322	| Code unlocks one steal for that game; computer's mark becomes the player's; counts as the move | Unit (`game.steal`, `handle_move`) and system test: play a game over HTTP with tokens, steal, see the cell become X and the computer reply. Preview: type the code, steal with mouse and with keyboard. |
323	| One steal per game | Unit and system: a second steal with the returned token → 400 "already stolen". |
324	| Never shown or hinted at until the code; then clear how to use it | Preview: page before the code is identical to today (no button, no column, no label change); after the code the panel, text and announcement appear. |

# Spec: a secret cheat code (`cheat-code`)

Source: `changes/cheat-code/intent.md`. This is the design to build from.
It describes the change against the system as it is today
(`docs/architecture.md`, `tictactoe/`).

## Summary

Against the computer, typing ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A on the page unlocks a
**steal** for the current game: once per game the player may turn one of
the computer's O squares into an X, and that is the player's move. A win
that used a steal is announced as "You won... with a little help" and
counted in its own score column, never as a normal win.

The browser recognises the code and shows the steal controls. The server
judges every steal. To enforce "one steal per game" without keeping state,
the server signs each game position it hands out (an HMAC **game token**)
and accepts a steal only together with a valid token that says no steal has
been used. Requests without a token behave exactly as today.

## How it works today (the parts this change touches)

- A board is 9 cells, `"X"`, `"O"` or `""`. Whose turn it is follows from
  the counts: `game.turn()` is X when X count == O count. `game.validate()`
  accepts a board only if X count − O count is 0 or 1.
- `POST /api/move` takes the whole board, `cell`, `mode`, `level`. Against
  the computer the player is X and the board must have X to move. The server
  plays `cell`, then the computer's reply, and answers the new board.
- The server trusts nothing: any board that passes `validate()` is accepted.
  It has no idea whether that board came from a real game.
- The score (X wins, O wins, draws) lives in `app.js` until reload.

## New and changed rules

1. **Steal.** In a game against the computer, on the player's turn (X to
   move, game still playing), the player may name one cell that holds `"O"`.
   That cell becomes `"X"`. This is the player's move: the computer then
   replies as usual if the game goes on.
2. **Once per game.** A game has at most one steal. A game is one unbroken
   chain of positions handed out by the server, starting from the empty
   board (see "Game token").
3. **Only against the computer**, at both levels (`easy`, `hard`). Never in
   `friend` mode.
4. **Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so the
   counts no longer say whose turn it is. The rule becomes: with `s` steals
   used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `s`,
   otherwise O. A valid board has X count − O count equal to `s` or `s + 1`.
   With `s = 0` both rules are exactly today's.
5. **A steal can win at once.** If the stolen square completes a line of X,
   the game is won by X and the computer does not move. A steal never fills
   an empty square, so it cannot cause a draw by itself.
6. **Assisted win.** A game won by X in which a steal was used is an
   *assisted* win. The server says so in every answer (`assisted: true`).
   The page announces it as "You won... with a little help" and counts it
   only in the "With help" column, not in "X wins".
7. After a steal the game goes on normally: the computer (either level)
   plays its best/random move from the new position, and the computer can
   still win or draw. Those are counted as today (O win, draw).
8. **The code.** ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A (`ArrowUp ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowDown
   ArrowLeft ArrowRight ArrowLeft ArrowRight b a`, B and A in either case).
   The code is recognised by the page only; it unlocks the steal controls
   for the current game. The server does not check the code (see Open
   questions 1).

## Game token (how the server enforces the rules without state)

The server keeps nothing between requests. Instead it signs what it must
trust when the browser sends it back, as `CLAUDE.md` allows.

- **Key.** `TICTACTOE_SECRET` from the environment (UTF-8 bytes) when set
  and not empty; otherwise 32 random bytes from `secrets.token_bytes` made
  once when the process starts. Production sets it through `ops/deploy.sh`
  and keeps it across releases, so tokens survive a deploy. The key is
  never logged, never sent, never put in an error message.
- **Format.** `"<s>.<mac>"`, where `<s>` is the number of steals used (`0`
  or `1`) and `<mac>` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the message
  `tictactoe-game-v1|<level>|<s>|<cells>`, with `<cells>` the 9 cells, each
  written as `X`, `O` or `-`. Example: `"0.3f9a…c1"` (64 hex digits).
  The token binds the board, the level and the steal count together;
  change any of them and it no longer verifies.
- **Checking.** Compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. A token that is not a
  string, has the wrong shape, an `<s>` other than `0`/`1`, or a MAC that
  does not match the request's `board` and `level` is rejected with
  `400 {"error": "the game token does not match this game"}`. This applies
  to any request that carries a `game` field, steal or not.
- **When the server hands one out** (the `game` field of the answer), only
  in `computer` mode and only while the game is still `playing`:
  - the request carried a valid token: the new position gets a token with
    the same `s` (or `s = 1` if this request was the steal);
  - the request had no token and its board was empty (first move of a new
    game): the new position gets a token with `s = 0`;
  - otherwise (no token, board not empty, e.g. a hand-made mid-game board
    or an older page): `game` is `null`. That game plays exactly as today
    and can never steal.
  So a token proves that the position was reached by legal moves through
  this server from an empty board, with `s` steals on the way.
- **Why this stops a second steal, even by hand.** A steal needs a token
  with `s = 0`. The answer to a steal only ever carries `s = 1` tokens, and
  every later answer in that game keeps `s = 1`. A board that has had a
  steal has X − O == 1 on X's turn, which no `s = 0` token can match and
  which `validate()` rejects without a token. Forging an `s = 0` token
  needs the key.
- **Replays.** Because the server is stateless, an old token stays valid.
  A player who kept an `s = 0` token from earlier in the same game can go
  back to that position and steal from there. That is a branch of the game
  (like an undo), and every branch still has at most one steal. Accepted
  (Open questions 3).

## API changes

`POST /api/move` keeps its path, limits (1024-byte body, 411, 413, 404,
405) and every existing field and error. New, all optional in the request:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `steal` | A cell 0–8 to steal, sent **instead of** `cell`. |
| `game` | The `game` token from the server's previous answer. |

New in every `200` answer (all modes):

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `game` | Token for the new position, or `null` (rules above). |
| `stealable` | Cells the player could steal now: the O cells when this answer has a token with `s = 0`, the game is playing and X is to move; otherwise `[]`. |
| `steal_used` | `true` once a steal has been used in this game (`s = 1`), else `false`. |
| `assisted` | `true` when `status` is `won`, `winner` is `X` and `steal_used` is `true`; else `false`. |

The page uses `stealable`, `steal_used` and `assisted` as given; it never
works out for itself which squares can be stolen or whether a win was
assisted.

### Examples (Hard; tokens shortened)

First move of a new game, no token (the existing request, unchanged):

```json
{"board": ["", "", "", "", "", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 0, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard"}
```

```json
{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "status": "playing",
 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 4,
 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [4], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
```

Next move, sending the token back:

```json
{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 8, "mode": "computer",
 "level": "hard", "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
```

```json
{"board": ["X", "O", "", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"], "status": "playing",
 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 1,
 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [1, 4], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
```

The steal: taking the centre completes the diagonal 0-4-8.

```json
{"board": ["X", "O", "", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"], "steal": 4, "mode": "computer",
 "level": "hard", "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
```

```json
{"board": ["X", "O", "", "", "X", "", "", "", "X"], "status": "won",
 "winner": "X", "line": [0, 4, 8], "turn": null, "computer_move": null,
 "game": null, "stealable": [], "steal_used": true, "assisted": true}
```

A steal that does not win (stealing cell 1 instead) gets the computer's
reply and an `s = 1` token; X is to move with X − O == 1. (Hard must block
row 0 at cell 2; this reply is the expected one, not recorded from code.)

```json
{"board": ["X", "X", "O", "", "O", "", "", "", "X"], "status": "playing",
 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 2,
 "game": "1.<64 hex>", "stealable": [], "steal_used": true, "assisted": false}
```

A friend game answers `game: null, stealable: [], steal_used: false,
assisted: false` in addition to today's fields.

### New errors (all `400 {"error": "..."}`)

Checked in this order, after today's checks of the body, `board` shape,
`mode` and `level`:

| Case | Message |
|------|---------|
| `game` present but not valid for this `board` and `level` (any request) | `the game token does not match this game` |
| both `cell` and `steal` present | `send either cell or steal, not both` |
| `steal` in `friend` mode | `you can only steal from the computer` |
| `steal` without `game` | `a steal needs the game token from the last answer` |
| `steal` with a token whose `s` is 1 | `you have already stolen a square in this game` |
| `steal` not a whole number 0–8 (`true` is not a number) | `steal must be a whole number from 0 to 8` |
| game already over | `the game is over` (today's message) |
| the cell is not an O (empty or X) | `you can only steal one of the computer's squares` |

The board check uses the token's `s`: a board with X − O outside
`s`..`s + 1` is rejected with today's message `X moves first and the
players alternate`, and with X − O ≠ `s` against the computer with today's
`against the computer you play X`.

## Logging (to see steals in production)

The intent will judge success by steals in games "we did not set up". The
server has no database, so after every successful steal the request handler
writes one line through `log_message` (stderr, which `ops/deploy.sh` sends
to `production/server.log`, next to the request line with the client
address):

```text
steal level=hard cell=4 status=won assisted=true
```

Nothing else is logged: no token, no key, no board. Because a steal needs a
token chain that started from an empty board, every logged steal happened
in a real game played through the server.

## The page

### Before the code (unchanged)

The page looks and behaves exactly as today: no steal button, no hint, no
"With help" column, no change to labels or status texts. The new elements
exist in `index.html` with `hidden` and are not shown or announced.

### Recognising the code

- `app.js` listens to `keydown` on `document` and keeps the last 10 keys.
  When they equal the code, the code is typed. A sliding window means extra
  keys before it do not matter (↑ ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ … still works).
- Ignored: events with Ctrl, Alt or Meta held, and auto-repeat
  (`event.repeat`). Keys typed while focus is in a `<select>` are not
  recorded (arrows there change the mode or level, which starts a new game).
- The board's own arrow handling stays as it is: typing the code with the
  focus on the board moves the focus around, which is harmless; arrows never
  play a move.
- The code unlocks only when the mode is `computer` and the game is
  `playing`. Otherwise it does nothing at all (friend mode: no message, no
  hint).
- Unlocking lasts for the current game. A new game (button, mode or level
  change) locks it again; typing the code again unlocks it again.

### After the code

- The status line (`aria-live`) announces: "Cheat unlocked! Once this game,
  you may steal one of the computer's squares." The current status text
  follows after the next move as usual.
- A panel under the status line appears with a **Steal a square** button
  (`aria-pressed`) and the short text "Press Steal, then choose an O. Esc
  cancels." The button is disabled-looking (`aria-disabled="true"`, still
  focusable) when `stealable` is empty, with the reason in the panel text:
  "No O to steal yet" before the computer has moved, "Steal used" after.
- The score table shows a fourth column **With help** (and keeps showing it
  until the page is reloaded, so the count stays visible).

### Steal mode

- Pressing the button (click, Enter, Space) turns steal mode on, but only
  if `stealable` is not empty. The status line says "Steal: choose one of
  the computer's squares." The focus moves to the lowest stealable square
  (roving `tabindex` as today).
- In steal mode only the squares in `stealable` are active
  (`aria-disabled="false"`, class `stealable` with a visible dashed outline
  that does not rely on colour alone). Their label gains ", can be stolen",
  e.g. "Row 2, column 2, O, can be stolen". Every other square is
  `aria-disabled="true"` and does nothing when chosen.
- Choosing a stealable square (click, tap, Enter, Space) sends
  `{board, steal, mode, level, game}`. Steal mode ends with the answer.
- Esc, or pressing the button again, ends steal mode without a move and
  puts the focus back on the button.
- Outside steal mode, clicking an O does nothing, as today.

### After a steal

- The status line says "You stole row R, column C." when the game goes on
  (then the usual "Your turn (X)" once the next answer arrives; moving the
  focus with the arrow keys keeps the message), and "You won... with
  a little help" when the steal or a later move wins with `assisted: true`.
- Score: `assisted: true` adds 1 to **With help** and nothing to X wins.
  A computer win or a draw after a steal counts as today.
- The panel says "Steal used" and the button stays disabled-looking.

### Small screens

The panel and the four-column score table must fit 320 px wide with no
horizontal scroll: the column headings are short ("X wins", "O wins",
"Draws", "With help") and the button is at least 44 px tall. The code
needs a keyboard, so phones without one cannot unlock it (Open questions 2).

## Modules

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `game.py` | `turn(board, steals=0)`, `validate(board, steals=0)`, `play(board, cell, steals=0)` follow rule 4. New `steal(board, cell, steals) -> list[str]`: checks and errors from the table above (already stolen, cell type, game over, not X's turn, not an O); returns a new board, never changes its input. New `check_cells(board)`: only the shape and cell checks of `validate` (which now calls it), so the server can check a board's shape before it knows the token's `s`. `outcome()` and `legal_moves()` do not change. |
| `ai.py` | `choose_move(board, level, rng=None, *, steals=0)`; `best_move` and `value` take `steals` too (still cached), so the search uses the right turn after a steal. With `steals=0` the moves are exactly today's. |
| new `signing.py` | The key (env or random at import, as above), `sign(board, level, steals) -> str`, `verify(token, board, level) -> int` (returns `s`, raises `IllegalMoveError`). Nothing else imports `os.environ`. |
| `server.py` | `handle_move` reads `game` and `steal`, verifies, plays the move or the steal, then the computer's reply with the right `steals`, and adds `game`, `stealable`, `steal_used`, `assisted`. `describe()` takes `steals`. `do_POST` writes the steal log line. Signature `handle_move(request)` stays. |
| `static/index.html` | Hidden cheat panel (button + text) under the status line; hidden "With help" column in the score table. |
| `static/app.js` | Code recognition, unlock state per game, steal mode, sending `game` back with every move, the new status texts, the fourth score counter. |
| `static/style.css` | `.stealable` outline, panel layout, small-screen fit. |
| `docs/architecture.md` | Updated in phase 3: the token, the new fields and errors, the turn rule, `signing.py`, the page's cheat. |

## What must keep working exactly as before

- Every request without `steal` and without `game` gets the same `board`,
  `status`, `winner`, `line`, `turn`, `computer_move` and the same errors
  as today; the only difference is the four added fields.
- Hard is unchanged for `steals=0` and never loses to fair play
  (`test_hard_never_loses` passes untouched). Easy is unchanged.
- Friend mode, `/health` (`200 ok`), the assets, 404/405/411/413, the
  1024-byte limit, the keyboard model of the board and its labels.
- All existing tests pass without change.

## How each line of the intent will be checked

| Intent line | Check |
|-------------|-------|
| Code unlocks one steal for that game; computer's mark becomes the player's; counts as the move | Unit (`game.steal`, `handle_move`) and system test: play a game over HTTP with tokens, steal, see the cell become X and the computer reply. Preview: type the code, steal with mouse and with keyboard. |
| One steal per game | Unit and system: a second steal with the returned token → 400 "already stolen". |
| Never shown or hinted at until the code; then clear how to use it | Preview: page before the code is identical to today (no button, no column, no label change); after the code the panel, text and announcement appear. |
| The code is ↑↑↓↓←→←→BA | Preview: the exact code unlocks; a wrong key in the middle does not; the sliding window works; uppercase B A works. |

   are "with help".

# System test report: `cheat-code`

Phase 5 of `docs/process.md`. The real server was started as production
starts it (`python3 -m tictactoe --port 0`, its own process) and driven over
HTTP only. The page (code recognition, steal mode, labels, score column) is
browser behaviour and was checked by a person in `preview.md`; it is not
repeated here.

## Result

**Whole suite: 215 passed** (`python3 -m pytest -q`, 0.65 s), unit and
system tests together. `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` are clean.
No server process is left running afterwards.

**Bugs found: none.** No code in `tictactoe/` was changed in this phase.

## What changed in `tests/system/`

- New `client.py`: `serve()`, a context manager that starts the server on
  port 0, waits for `/health`, yields the base URL and **always** stops the
  process in `finally` (terminate, then kill if it has not stopped after
  5 s), even when a test fails. It can set `TICTACTOE_SECRET` (and always
  removes any inherited value otherwise) and send stderr to a file. Also
  `get()` and `post()`, moved here from `test_http.py`.
- `test_http.py`: now uses `client.py`. Its tests are unchanged.
- New `test_cheat.py`: a module-scoped server started with a known
  `TICTACTOE_SECRET`, as production does, with its log (stderr) written to a
  temporary file.

## What was tested (`test_cheat.py`)

The steal, end to end:

| Test | Shows |
|------|-------|
| `test_the_first_move_of_a_game_gets_a_token` | A tokenless first move from the empty board gets an `s = 0` token; `stealable` is the computer's O. |
| `test_a_steal_that_wins_at_once_is_an_assisted_win` | Hard: X 0, O 4, X 8, O 1, then steal 4. The whole answer is exactly the spec's example: won by X on 0-4-8, no computer move, `game: null`, `steal_used` and `assisted` true. |
| `test_a_steal_is_the_players_move_and_the_computer_replies` | Steal 1 instead: the cell becomes X, the computer replies (blocks at 2, as the spec expected), X to move, `1.` token, `stealable: []`. |
| `test_after_a_steal_the_game_plays_on_to_its_end` | After a steal the game goes on with `1.` tokens to its end; `assisted` is true only if X won. |
| `test_a_steal_works_at_easy` (3 openings) | The steal works at Easy too. |
| `test_the_stealable_squares_are_the_os_on_the_players_turn` | Through a whole game, `stealable` always lists exactly the O cells, and is empty once the game is over. |

Nobody can steal twice, even by hand:

| Test | Request | Answer |
|------|---------|--------|
| `test_a_second_steal_is_refused` | a steal with the `1.` token from the first steal | 400 `you have already stolen a square in this game` |
| `test_a_steal_needs_a_token` | a steal with no token | 400 `a steal needs the game token from the last answer` |
| `test_a_stolen_board_without_its_token_is_refused` | the board after a steal, sent with no token | 400 `against the computer you play X` |
| `test_the_token_is_bound_to_the_board` | a valid token with a different board | 400 `the game token does not match this game` |
| `test_the_token_is_bound_to_the_level` | a valid Hard token with `level: easy` | same 400 |
| `test_editing_the_steal_count_breaks_the_token` | `1.` changed to `0.` by hand (to steal again), and `0.` changed to `1.` | same 400 |
| `test_a_malformed_or_forged_token_is_refused` (10 cases) | `""`, `"0"`, `"0."`, `s = 2`, a zero MAC, an uppercase-hex MAC, the number 0, `true`, a list, an object | same 400 |
| `test_a_hand_made_mid_game_board_gets_no_token` | a tokenless mid-game board | 200 with `game: null`, `stealable: []`, so that game can never steal |
| `test_a_token_survives_a_restart_with_the_same_secret` | a token from this server, sent to a fresh server with the same `TICTACTOE_SECRET` and then to one with a different secret | first accepted (as across a deploy), second refused with the mismatch 400 |

Other refusals: a steal in friend mode (400 `you can only steal from the
computer`); `cell` and `steal` together (400 `send either cell or steal, not
both`); stealing an empty square or an X (400 `you can only steal one of the
computer's squares`); `steal` of 9, -1, `true`, `"4"`, `4.0` (400 `steal must
be a whole number from 0 to 8`).

The old game, unchanged:

- `test_a_friend_game_gets_no_token`: friend answers carry `game: null,
  stealable: [], steal_used: false, assisted: false`.
- `test_a_tokenless_game_against_hard_still_never_lets_x_win`: all 9
  openings for X, played to the end without tokens: X never wins.
- `test_tokenless_errors_are_todays`: today's messages for the wrong turn,
  bad alternation and a bad level.
- All tests in `test_http.py` (health, page and assets, 404s, a whole game
  against Hard, a friend game, bad moves, 413) pass unchanged.

What the server prints:

- `test_a_steal_is_logged_without_the_key_or_any_token`: after a winning
  steal, the server log has `steal level=hard cell=4 status=won
  assisted=true`. Neither the secret nor the token (nor its MAC) appears
  anywhere in the log of the whole test module.

## A comparison with the server before the change (by hand, not in the suite)

To back "the old game behaves exactly as before" with more than the fixed
cases above, the baseline package (commit `09325b7`, before this change) was
pulled from git and run as a second server next to the current one. 2318
tokenless requests were sent to both: 2000 random boards (any mix of X, O
and empty, cells -1 to 9, both modes, Hard), 300 random friend moves, all 9
first moves against Hard, and malformed bodies (`null`, `[]`, `3`, `cell:
true`, no cell, a bad board, a bad mode, a bad level, `game` and `steal` sent
as `null`). Easy was left out because its moves are random.

Result: **0 differences**. 275 of the requests were answered 200, and every
field of the old answer was the same in the new one (the new one only adds
the four new fields). The other 2043 got the same status and the same error
message. This script is not in the suite because it needs the git history.

## Notes for the code review (not bugs)

- A token from a computer game is also accepted in friend mode, as the spec
  says ("any request that carries a `game` field"). With a `1.` token the
  friend move uses the after-steal turn rule and the answer says
  `steal_used: true`, with `game: null`. The page never sends this, and it
  cannot give a second steal or a new token, so it does no harm. Worth a
  look if the reviewer would rather refuse `game` in friend mode.
- Replaying an older `0.` token to steal from an earlier position works, as
  the spec accepts (Open questions 3). No test asserts it either way.

+"""The game token: a signed position, so the server can stay stateless.
+
+A token is "<s>.<mac>", where <s> is the number of steals used in the game
+(0 or 1) and <mac> is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, under the server's
+key, of the level, <s> and the board. The server hands one out with each
+position it answers and accepts it back only for that exact position.
+
+The key is TICTACTOE_SECRET when it is set, otherwise random bytes made at
+start-up. It never leaves this module.
+"""
+
+import hashlib
+import hmac
+import os
+import re
+import secrets
+
+from .game import IllegalMoveError
+
+_KEY = os.environ.get("TICTACTOE_SECRET", "").encode() or secrets.token_bytes(32)
+_SHAPE = re.compile(r"[01]\.[0-9a-f]{64}")
+_MISMATCH = "the game token does not match this game"
+
+
+def _mac(board: list[str], level: str, steals: int) -> str:
+    cells = "".join(cell or "-" for cell in board)
+    message = f"tictactoe-game-v1|{level}|{steals}|{cells}".encode()
+    return hmac.new(_KEY, message, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
+
+
+def sign(board: list[str], level: str, steals: int) -> str:
+    """The token for `board` at `level` with `steals` steals used."""
+    return f"{steals}.{_mac(board, level, steals)}"
+
+
+def verify(token: object, board: list[str], level: str) -> int:
+    """The steals a token for `board` at `level` carries; raises if it does not match."""
+    if not isinstance(token, str) or not _SHAPE.fullmatch(token):
+        raise IllegalMoveError(_MISMATCH)
+    steals = int(token[0])
+    if not hmac.compare_digest(token[2:], _mac(board, level, steals)):
+        raise IllegalMoveError(_MISMATCH)
+    return steals

1	"""The rules of tic-tac-toe.
2	
3	A board is a list of 9 cells, row by row, each "X", "O" or "" (empty).
4	X always moves first, so whose turn it is follows from the board itself.
5	"""
6	
7	from dataclasses import dataclass
8	
9	EMPTY = ""
10	SIZE = 9
11	MARKS = ("X", "O")
12	LINES = (
13	    (0, 1, 2),
14	    (3, 4, 5),
15	    (6, 7, 8),
16	    (0, 3, 6),
17	    (1, 4, 7),
18	    (2, 5, 8),
19	    (0, 4, 8),
20	    (2, 4, 6),
21	)
22	
23	
24	class IllegalMoveError(ValueError):
25	    """A move or a board that the rules do not allow."""
26	
27	
28	@dataclass(frozen=True)
29	class Outcome:
30	    """Where a game stands: "playing", "won" or "draw"."""
31	
32	    status: str
33	    winner: str | None = None
34	    line: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None
35	
36	
37	def new_board() -> list[str]:
38	    return [EMPTY] * SIZE
39	
40	
41	def winning_line(board: list[str]) -> tuple[str, tuple[int, int, int]] | None:
42	    for line in LINES:
43	        a, b, c = (board[i] for i in line)
44	        if a and a == b == c:
45	            return a, line
46	    return None
47	
48	
49	def outcome(board: list[str]) -> Outcome:
50	    if found := winning_line(board):
51	        return Outcome("won", found[0], found[1])
52	    if all(board):
53	        return Outcome("draw")
54	    return Outcome("playing")
55	
56	
57	def turn(board: list[str], steals: int = 0) -> str:
58	    """The mark that moves next, with `steals` steals used in the game.
59	
60	    A steal turns an O into an X without adding a mark, so X is to move when
61	    X count - O count equals `steals`.
62	    """
63	    return "X" if board.count("X") - board.count("O") == steals else "O"
64	
65	
66	def legal_moves(board: list[str]) -> list[int]:
67	    if outcome(board).status != "playing":
68	        return []
69	    return [i for i, cell in enumerate(board) if not cell]
70	
71	
72	def check_cells(board: object) -> list[str]:
73	    """Check only the shape and the cells of a board from outside, not the counts."""
74	    if not isinstance(board, list) or len(board) != SIZE:
75	        raise IllegalMoveError("board must be a list of 9 cells")
76	    if any(cell not in (*MARKS, EMPTY) for cell in board):
77	        raise IllegalMoveError('cells must be "X", "O" or ""')
78	    return list(board)
79	
80	
81	def validate(board: object, steals: int = 0) -> list[str]:
82	    """Check a board that came from outside and return it as a clean list."""
83	    board = check_cells(board)
84	    x, o = board.count("X"), board.count("O")
85	    if x - o not in (steals, steals + 1):
86	        raise IllegalMoveError("X moves first and the players alternate")
87	    return board
88	
89	
90	def play(board: list[str], cell: object, steals: int = 0) -> list[str]:
91	    """The board after the player to move takes `cell`. Does not change `board`."""
92	    # bool is a subclass of int, but true is not a square
93	    if not isinstance(cell, int) or isinstance(cell, bool) or not 0 <= cell < SIZE:
94	        raise IllegalMoveError("cell must be a whole number from 0 to 8")
95	    if outcome(board).status != "playing":
96	        raise IllegalMoveError("the game is over")
97	    if board[cell]:
98	        raise IllegalMoveError("that square is taken")
99	    after = list(board)
100	    after[cell] = turn(board, steals)
101	    return after
102	
103	
104	def steal(board: list[str], cell: object, steals: int) -> list[str]:
105	    """The board after X takes the computer's O on `cell`. Does not change `board`.
106	
107	    A steal is X's move, allowed once per game: `steals` is how many steals
108	    the game has used so far.
109	    """
110	    if steals >= 1:
111	        raise IllegalMoveError("you have already stolen a square in this game")
112	    # bool is a subclass of int, but true is not a square
113	    if not isinstance(cell, int) or isinstance(cell, bool) or not 0 <= cell < SIZE:
114	        raise IllegalMoveError("steal must be a whole number from 0 to 8")
115	    if outcome(board).status != "playing":
116	        raise IllegalMoveError("the game is over")
117	    if turn(board, steals) != "X":
118	        raise IllegalMoveError("against the computer you play X")
119	    if board[cell] != "O":
120	        raise IllegalMoveError("you can only steal one of the computer's squares")
121	    after = list(board)
122	    after[cell] = "X"
123	    return after

"""The game token: a signed position, so the server can stay stateless.

A token is "<s>.<mac>", where <s> is the number of steals used in the game
(0 or 1) and <mac> is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, under the server's
key, of the level, <s> and the board. The server hands one out with each
position it answers and accepts it back only for that exact position.

The key is TICTACTOE_SECRET when it is set, otherwise random bytes made at
start-up. It never leaves this module.
"""

import hashlib
import hmac
import os
import re
import secrets

from .game import IllegalMoveError

_KEY = os.environ.get("TICTACTOE_SECRET", "").encode() or secrets.token_bytes(32)
_SHAPE = re.compile(r"[01]\.[0-9a-f]{64}")
_MISMATCH = "the game token does not match this game"


def _mac(board: list[str], level: str, steals: int) -> str:
    cells = "".join(cell or "-" for cell in board)
    message = f"tictactoe-game-v1|{level}|{steals}|{cells}".encode()
    return hmac.new(_KEY, message, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def sign(board: list[str], level: str, steals: int) -> str:
    """The token for `board` at `level` with `steals` steals used."""
    return f"{steals}.{_mac(board, level, steals)}"


def verify(token: object, board: list[str], level: str) -> int:
    """The steals a token for `board` at `level` carries; raises if it does not match."""
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not _SHAPE.fullmatch(token):
        raise IllegalMoveError(_MISMATCH)
    steals = int(token[0])
    if not hmac.compare_digest(token[2:], _mac(board, level, steals)):
        raise IllegalMoveError(_MISMATCH)
    return steals

1	"""The computer player.
2	
3	Hard plays perfectly (negamax over the whole game tree, which is small
4	enough to search every move), so it never loses. Easy wins when it sees a
5	winning move and otherwise plays at random, which a casual player can beat.
6	
7	`steals` is how many steals the game has used (see `game.turn`): a steal
8	changes whose turn the counts say it is, so the search needs it too.
9	"""
10	
11	import random
12	from functools import cache
13	
14	from . import game
15	
16	LEVELS = ("easy", "hard")
17	WIN = 10
18	
19	
20	def choose_move(
21	    board: list[str], level: str, rng: random.Random | None = None, *, steals: int = 0
22	) -> int:
23	    """The cell the computer plays for whoever's turn it is on `board`."""
24	    if level not in LEVELS:
25	        raise game.IllegalMoveError(f"level must be one of: {', '.join(LEVELS)}")
26	    moves = game.legal_moves(board)
27	    if not moves:
28	        raise game.IllegalMoveError("the game is over")
29	    if level == "hard":
30	        return best_move(tuple(board), steals)
31	    me = game.turn(board, steals)
32	    for cell in moves:
33	        if game.outcome(game.play(board, cell, steals)).winner == me:
34	            return cell
35	    return (rng or random).choice(moves)
36

38	@cache
39	def best_move(board: tuple[str, ...], steals: int = 0) -> int:
40	    """The best cell for the player to move; the lowest cell among equals."""
41	    moves = game.legal_moves(list(board))
42	    return max(
43	        moves,
44	        key=lambda cell: (-value(tuple(game.play(list(board), cell, steals)), steals), -cell),
45	    )
46	
47	
48	@cache
49	def value(board: tuple[str, ...], steals: int = 0) -> int:
50	    """How good `board` is for the player to move: positive wins, 0 draws.
51	
52	    A win is worth more the sooner it comes, so Hard wins quickly and loses
53	    (never, in practice) as late as possible.
54	    """
55	    result = game.outcome(list(board))
56	    if result.status == "won":
57	        return -(WIN - (9 - board.count(game.EMPTY)))
58	    if result.status == "draw":
59	        return 0
60	    return max(
61	        -value(tuple(game.play(list(board), c, steals)), steals)
62	        for c in game.legal_moves(list(board))
63	    )

1	# Architecture
2	
3	```text
4	browser (static/)                          server (Python, stdlib)
5	┌───────────────────────┐  POST /api/move  ┌────────────────────────────┐
6	│ index.html  app.js    │ ───────────────▶ │ server.py  handle_move()   │
7	│ draws, sends clicks,  │    whole board   │   ├─ game.py  rules        │
8	│ keeps the score       │ ◀─────────────── │   └─ ai.py    computer     │
9	└───────────────────────┘   new board +    └────────────────────────────┘
10	                            outcome
11	```
12	
13	The rules live in Python only. The browser never decides whether a move is
14	legal or who won: it shows what the server answers.
15	
16	## Modules (`tictactoe/`)
17	
18	| File | Job |
19	|------|-----|
20	| `game.py` | The rules. A board is a list of 9 cells, row by row, each `"X"`, `"O"` or `""`. X moves first, so `turn(board, steals=0)` follows from the counts: with `steals` steals used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `steals`. `check_cells(board)` checks only a board's shape and cells, `validate(board, steals=0)` checks a whole board from outside (`check_cells`, then X − O must be `steals` or `steals + 1`), `play(board, cell, steals=0)` returns a new board (never changes its input) or raises `IllegalMoveError`, `steal(board, cell, steals)` returns a new board with the O on `cell` turned into an X (once per game, on X's turn, only an O), `outcome()` says `playing`, `won` (with winner and line) or `draw`. With `steals=0` everything is the plain game. |
21	| `ai.py` | The computer. `choose_move(board, level, rng=None, *, steals=0)`: **hard** is negamax over the full game tree, cached (per board and `steals`), lowest cell among equals, so it is deterministic and never loses; **easy** takes a winning move if it sees one, otherwise plays at random. `steals` is passed on to every rule call, so the search knows whose turn it is after a steal. |
22	| `signing.py` | The game token. The key is `TICTACTOE_SECRET` when set and not empty, otherwise 32 random bytes made at start-up; it is the only module that reads `os.environ`, and the key never leaves it. `sign(board, level, steals)` returns `"<s>.<mac>"`, the HMAC-SHA256 (lowercase hex) of `tictactoe-game-v1|<level>|<s>|<cells>`, cells written `X`, `O` or `-`. `verify(token, board, level)` returns `s`, or raises `IllegalMoveError("the game token does not match this game")`; it compares with `hmac.compare_digest`. |
23	| `server.py` | `ThreadingHTTPServer`. Serves a fixed map of assets (no request path reaches the file system), `/health`, and the move API (`handle_move`, with `check_steal_request` for requests that carry a token or a steal). Keeps no state: what it must trust it signs with `signing.py`. Logs one line per successful steal. |
24	| `__main__.py` | `python3 -m tictactoe [--host] [--port]`; prints the URL it listens on. |
25	| `static/` | `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`. No build step, no libraries. |
26	
27	## The move API
28	
29	`POST /api/move`, a JSON body of at most 1024 bytes:
30	
31	```json
32	{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 2, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard",
33	 "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
34	```
35	
36	- `mode` is `computer` (default) or `friend`; `level` is `easy` or `hard`
37	  (default), used only against the computer.
38	- Against the computer the player is always X, so the board must have X
39	  to move.
40	- The server plays `cell` for whoever is to move, then, against the
41	  computer and if the game goes on, the computer's reply as O.
42	- `game` (optional) is the token from the previous answer. `steal`
43	  (optional, instead of `cell`) is a cell holding an O that the player
44	  turns into an X, as their move: once per game, only against the computer,
45	  and only together with a `game` token. A field sent as `null` counts as
46	  not sent.
47	
48	Answer `200`:
49	
50	```json
51	{"board": ["X", "", "X", "", "O", "", "", "", "O"], "status": "playing",
52	 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 8,
53	 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [4, 8], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
54	```
55	
56	`status` is `playing`, `won` or `draw`; `line` is the three winning cells;
57	`turn` is `null` once the game is over; `computer_move` is `null` when the
58	computer did not move. `game` is the token for the new position (below) or
59	`null`; `stealable` lists the O cells when the answer's token has `s = 0`,
60	the game is playing and X is to move, else `[]`; `steal_used` is `true`
61	once the game has used its steal; `assisted` is `true` for a win by X with
62	`steal_used`. The page uses these as given and works out none of them.
63	
64	### The game token, and why the server stays stateless
65	
66	To allow one steal per game without remembering games, the server signs
67	each position it hands out (`signing.py`): the token `"<s>.<mac>"` binds
68	the board, the level and `s`, the steals used so far. It is handed out
69	only in `computer` mode while the game is `playing`: with the request's
70	`s` (or `1` after a steal) when the request carried a valid token, with
71	`s = 0` when the request had no token and an empty board (a new game), and
72	otherwise `game` is `null` (a hand-made mid-game board plays as before but
73	can never steal). A steal needs an `s = 0` token; after it every token in
74	that game has `s = 1`, and forging one needs the key. An old token stays
75	valid, so a player can go back to an earlier position of the same game
76	and steal there: a branch, which still has at most one steal.
77	
78	**Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so with
79	`s` steals used X is to move when X − O == `s`, and a valid board has
80	X − O equal to `s` or `s + 1`. With `s = 0` this is the plain rule.
81	
82	**Without `game` and `steal`** a request goes through exactly the old
83	checks and gets the old answer, plus the four new fields.
84	
85	Errors: `400 {"error": "..."}` for any bad input (bad JSON, impossible
86	board, taken square, game over, unknown mode or level), `411` without a
87	`Content-Length`, `413` for a body over 1024 bytes, `404` for other paths,
88	`405` for `GET /api/move`. A request with `game` or `steal` is checked in
89	this order: the body, the board's shape and cells, mode, level; then
90	
91	| Case | Message |
92	|------|---------|
93	| `game` does not verify for this `board` and `level` | `the game token does not match this game` |
94	| both `cell` and `steal` | `send either cell or steal, not both` |
95	| `steal` in `friend` mode | `you can only steal from the computer` |
96	| `steal` without `game` | `a steal needs the game token from the last answer` |
97	| X − O outside `s`..`s + 1` | `X moves first and the players alternate` |
98	| not X to move under `s`, against the computer | `against the computer you play X` |
99	| `steal` with an `s = 1` token | `you have already stolen a square in this game` |
100	| `steal` not a whole number 0–8 | `steal must be a whole number from 0 to 8` |
101	| the game is over | `the game is over` |
102	| the cell is not an O | `you can only steal one of the computer's squares` |
103	
104	A normal move with a token then gets `play`'s usual errors.
105	
106	**Log.** After each successful steal the server writes one line through
107	`log_message` (stderr), `steal level=hard cell=4 status=won assisted=true`,
108	and nothing else: no token, no key, no board.
109	
110	## The page
111	
112	`app.js` holds the current answer from the server and the score (X wins, O
113	wins, draws, and wins with help, until the page is reloaded). Each click or Enter/Space on a
114	square sends one move. The board is one tab stop: arrow keys, Home and End
115	move between squares (roving `tabindex`), and every square has an
116	`aria-label` such as "Row 1, column 3, X, winning". The status line is an
117	`aria-live` region. Changing mode or level starts a new game.
118	
119	`app.js` keeps the whole last answer, including `game`, `stealable`,
120	`steal_used` and `assisted`; a new game starts with `game: null`. Every
121	move request sends the last answer's `game` token back, and leaves it out
122	while it is `null` (the first move of a game, friend mode, a game that has
123	ended). An error, such as "the game token does not match this game" after a
124	development restart, shows in the status line, and New game recovers.
125	
126	`index.html` also holds the cheat panel under the status line (`#cheat`: the
127	"Steal a square" button `#steal` with `aria-pressed`, and the text
128	`#cheat-text`) and a fourth score column "With help" (`#score-help-head`,
