# Architecture

```text
browser (static/)                          server (Python, stdlib)
┌───────────────────────┐  POST /api/move  ┌────────────────────────────┐
│ index.html  app.js    │ ───────────────▶ │ server.py  handle_move()   │
│ draws, sends clicks,  │    whole board   │   ├─ game.py  rules        │
│ keeps the score       │ ◀─────────────── │   └─ ai.py    computer     │
└───────────────────────┘   new board +    └────────────────────────────┘
                            outcome
```

The rules live in Python only. The browser never decides whether a move is
legal or who won: it shows what the server answers.

## Modules (`tictactoe/`)

| File | Job |
|------|-----|
| `game.py` | The rules. A board is a list of 9 cells, row by row, each `"X"`, `"O"` or `""`. X moves first, so `turn(board, steals=0)` follows from the counts: with `steals` steals used in the game (0 or 1), X is to move when X count − O count == `steals`. `check_cells(board)` checks only a board's shape and cells, `validate(board, steals=0)` checks a whole board from outside (`check_cells`, then X − O must be `steals` or `steals + 1`), `play(board, cell, steals=0)` returns a new board (never changes its input) or raises `IllegalMoveError`, `steal(board, cell, steals)` returns a new board with the O on `cell` turned into an X (once per game, on X's turn, only an O), `outcome()` says `playing`, `won` (with winner and line) or `draw`. With `steals=0` everything is the plain game. |
| `ai.py` | The computer. `choose_move(board, level, rng=None, *, steals=0)`: **hard** is negamax over the full game tree, cached (per board and `steals`), lowest cell among equals, so it is deterministic and never loses; **easy** takes a winning move if it sees one, otherwise plays at random. `steals` is passed on to every rule call, so the search knows whose turn it is after a steal. |
| `signing.py` | The game token. The key is `TICTACTOE_SECRET` when set and not empty, otherwise 32 random bytes made at start-up; it is the only module that reads `os.environ`, and the key never leaves it. `sign(board, level, steals)` returns `"<s>.<mac>"`, the HMAC-SHA256 (lowercase hex) of `tictactoe-game-v1|<level>|<s>|<cells>`, cells written `X`, `O` or `-`. `verify(token, board, level)` returns `s`, or raises `IllegalMoveError("the game token does not match this game")`; it compares with `hmac.compare_digest`. |
| `server.py` | `ThreadingHTTPServer`. Serves a fixed map of assets (no request path reaches the file system), `/health`, and the move API (`handle_move`, with `check_steal_request` for requests that carry a token or a steal). Keeps no state: what it must trust it signs with `signing.py`. Logs one line per successful steal. |
| `__main__.py` | `python3 -m tictactoe [--host] [--port]`; prints the URL it listens on. |
| `static/` | `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`. No build step, no libraries. |

## The move API

`POST /api/move`, a JSON body of at most 1024 bytes:

```json
{"board": ["X", "", "", "", "O", "", "", "", ""], "cell": 2, "mode": "computer", "level": "hard",
 "game": "0.<64 hex>"}
```

- `mode` is `computer` (default) or `friend`; `level` is `easy` or `hard`
  (default), used only against the computer.
- Against the computer the player is always X, so the board must have X
  to move.
- The server plays `cell` for whoever is to move, then, against the
  computer and if the game goes on, the computer's reply as O.
- `game` (optional) is the token from the previous answer. `steal`
  (optional, instead of `cell`) is a cell holding an O that the player
  turns into an X, as their move: once per game, only against the computer,
  and only together with a `game` token. A field sent as `null` counts as
  not sent.

Answer `200`:

```json
{"board": ["X", "", "X", "", "O", "", "", "", "O"], "status": "playing",
 "winner": null, "line": null, "turn": "X", "computer_move": 8,
 "game": "0.<64 hex>", "stealable": [4, 8], "steal_used": false, "assisted": false}
```

`status` is `playing`, `won` or `draw`; `line` is the three winning cells;
`turn` is `null` once the game is over; `computer_move` is `null` when the
computer did not move. `game` is the token for the new position (below) or
`null`; `stealable` lists the O cells when the answer's token has `s = 0`,
the game is playing and X is to move, else `[]`; `steal_used` is `true`
once the game has used its steal; `assisted` is `true` for a win by X with
`steal_used`. The page uses these as given and works out none of them.

### The game token, and why the server stays stateless

To allow one steal per game without remembering games, the server signs
each position it hands out (`signing.py`): the token `"<s>.<mac>"` binds
the board, the level and `s`, the steals used so far. It is handed out
only in `computer` mode while the game is `playing`: with the request's
`s` (or `1` after a steal) when the request carried a valid token, with
`s = 0` when the request had no token and an empty board (a new game), and
otherwise `game` is `null` (a hand-made mid-game board plays as before but
can never steal). A steal needs an `s = 0` token; after it every token in
that game has `s = 1`, and forging one needs the key. An old token stays
valid, so a player can go back to an earlier position of the same game
and steal there: a branch, which still has at most one steal.

**Turn after a steal.** A steal changes a mark without adding one, so with
`s` steals used X is to move when X − O == `s`, and a valid board has
X − O equal to `s` or `s + 1`. With `s = 0` this is the plain rule.

**Without `game` and `steal`** a request goes through exactly the old
checks and gets the old answer, plus the four new fields.

Errors: `400 {"error": "..."}` for any bad input (bad JSON, impossible
board, taken square, game over, unknown mode or level), `411` without a
`Content-Length`, `413` for a body over 1024 bytes, `404` for other paths,
`405` for `GET /api/move`. A request with `game` or `steal` is checked in
this order: the body, the board's shape and cells, mode, level; then

| Case | Message |
|------|---------|
| `game` does not verify for this `board` and `level` | `the game token does not match this game` |
| both `cell` and `steal` | `send either cell or steal, not both` |
| `steal` in `friend` mode | `you can only steal from the computer` |
| `steal` without `game` | `a steal needs the game token from the last answer` |
| X − O outside `s`..`s + 1` | `X moves first and the players alternate` |
| not X to move under `s`, against the computer | `against the computer you play X` |
| `steal` with an `s = 1` token | `you have already stolen a square in this game` |
| `steal` not a whole number 0–8 | `steal must be a whole number from 0 to 8` |
| the game is over | `the game is over` |
| the cell is not an O | `you can only steal one of the computer's squares` |

A normal move with a token then gets `play`'s usual errors.

**Log.** After each successful steal the server writes one line through
`log_message` (stderr), `steal level=hard cell=4 status=won assisted=true`,
and nothing else: no token, no key, no board.

## The page

`app.js` holds the current answer from the server and the score (X wins, O
wins, draws, and wins with help, until the page is reloaded). Each click or Enter/Space on a
square sends one move. The board is one tab stop: arrow keys, Home and End
move between squares (roving `tabindex`), and every square has an
`aria-label` such as "Row 1, column 3, X, winning". The status line is an
`aria-live` region. Changing mode or level starts a new game.

`app.js` keeps the whole last answer, including `game`, `stealable`,
`steal_used` and `assisted`; a new game starts with `game: null`. Every
move request sends the last answer's `game` token back, and leaves it out
while it is `null` (the first move of a game, friend mode, a game that has
ended). An error, such as "the game token does not match this game" after a
development restart, shows in the status line, and New game recovers.

`index.html` also holds the cheat panel under the status line (`#cheat`: the
"Steal a square" button `#steal` with `aria-pressed`, and the text
`#cheat-text`) and a fourth score column "With help" (`#score-help-head`,
`#score-help`). All of them carry `hidden`, and `style.css` makes `hidden`
win over every display rule, so until the cheat is unlocked the page looks
and reads exactly as before. `style.css` styles them: a dashed frame on
`.cell.stealable` (shape, not colour alone), a steal button at least 44 px
tall, and tighter score cells once the fourth column shows, so it fits
320 px.

### The cheat code

- **Recognising it.** A `keydown` listener on `document` keeps the last 10
  keys and compares them with `ArrowUp ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowDown ArrowLeft
  ArrowRight ArrowLeft ArrowRight b a` (B and A in either case), so extra
  keys before the code do not matter. It ignores keys with Ctrl, Alt or
  Meta, auto-repeat, and keys typed in a `<select>`. The board's own arrow
  handling is unchanged: typing the code on the board only moves the focus.
  The code is plain in `app.js`: it is shared on purpose.
- **Locking per game.** The code unlocks only in `computer` mode while the
  game is `playing`; otherwise it does nothing at all. New game, a mode
  change or a level change locks it again and clears the keys. The server
  does not know about the code; it only judges steals.
- **Unlocking** shows the panel and the "With help" column and announces
  "Cheat unlocked! Once this game, you may steal one of the computer's
  squares." in the status line. Such messages (`notice` in `app.js`) stay
  until the next answer from the server, then the usual text returns.
- **The panel.** The button is `aria-disabled="true"` (still focusable)
  while the answer's `stealable` is empty, and the text says why: "No O to
  steal yet", or "Steal used" once `steal_used`. Otherwise it says "Press
  Steal, then choose an O. Esc cancels."
- **Steal mode.** The button (click, Enter, Space) turns it on only when
  `stealable` is not empty: `aria-pressed="true"`, the status says "Steal:
  choose one of the computer's squares.", and the focus moves to the lowest
  stealable square (roving `tabindex`). Only the squares in `stealable` are
  then `aria-disabled="false"`, with class `stealable` and ", can be stolen"
  in their label; every other square does nothing. Choosing one sends
  `{board, steal, mode, level, game}`. Steal mode ends with the answer (or
  an error), or with Esc or a second press of the button, which puts the
  focus back on the button. Outside steal mode an O does nothing, as before.
- **After a steal.** While the game goes on, the status says "You stole row
  R, column C.". An answer with `assisted: true` shows "You won... with a
  little help" and adds 1 to "With help", not to "X wins"; O wins and draws
  count as before. The column stays visible until the page is reloaded.
  `app.js` uses `stealable`, `steal_used` and `assisted` as the server sends
  them and works out no rule.

## Tests

- `tests/test_game.py`, `tests/test_ai.py`, `tests/test_server.py`: unit
  tests. `test_hard_never_loses` plays Hard against every possible opponent,
  as X and as O.
- `tests/system/test_http.py`: starts `python3 -m tictactoe --port 0` as a

  `play`, following spec rule 4. X is to move when X count − O count ==
  `steals`, and a valid board has X − O equal to `steals` or `steals + 1`.
  With `steals=0`, every result, error message and the order of the checks
  stay exactly as they are today. `outcome()` and `legal_moves()` do not
  change.
- [x] `tictactoe/game.py`: add `steal(board, cell, steals) -> list[str]`. It
  raises `IllegalMoveError` with the spec's exact messages, in the spec's
  order: `steals` already 1 ("you have already stolen a square in this
  game"), `cell` not a whole number 0–8 with `bool` refused ("steal must be a
  whole number from 0 to 8"), game over ("the game is over"), not X's turn
  under `steals` ("against the computer you play X"), cell not an `"O"`
  ("you can only steal one of the computer's squares"). It returns a new
  board with that cell set to `"X"` and never changes its input.
- [x] `tictactoe/ai.py`: add a keyword `steals=0` to
  `choose_move(board, level, rng=None, *, steals=0)` and an argument to
  `best_move` and `value`, so the `@cache` key includes it. Pass it to every
  `game.turn`, `game.play` and recursive call, including Easy's check for a
  winning move. With `steals=0` the moves must be exactly today's.

  describes. The key is `TICTACTOE_SECRET` encoded as UTF-8 when it is set
  and not empty, otherwise `secrets.token_bytes(32)`, made once at import.

  `O` or `-`. `verify(token, board, level) -> int` returns `s`. It raises

  token is not a `str`, does not have exactly the shape `0.`/`1.` followed
  by 64 lowercase hex digits, or has a MAC that does not match. It compares
  with `hmac.compare_digest`. The key never appears in a return value, an
  error or a log.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy tictactoe to production. Owned by the platform team: do not edit.
#
# Gates (tests, lint, review) -> release copy -> switch -> smoke test,
# rolling back to the previous release if the smoke test fails.
#
# Usage: ops/deploy.sh            deploy the working tree
#        ops/deploy.sh --status   show what is running
#        ops/deploy.sh --stop     stop production
# Env:   PROD_DIR  (default: ../production next to the repository)
#        PROD_PORT (default: 8088)

set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
PROD_DIR="${PROD_DIR:-$(dirname "${REPO}")/production}"
PROD_PORT="${PROD_PORT:-8088}"
PID_FILE="${PROD_DIR}/server.pid"
# One random key for the life of production, handed to every release as
# TICTACTOE_SECRET (see CLAUDE.md). Made once, never printed.
SECRET_FILE="${PROD_DIR}/secret"
URL="http://127.0.0.1:${PROD_PORT}"

step() { printf '\n==> %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() {
	printf 'DEPLOY FAILED: %s\n' "$*" >&2
	exit 1
}

running_pid() {
	local pid
	[[ -f "${PID_FILE}" ]] || return 1
	pid="$(cat "${PID_FILE}")"
	kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null && echo "${pid}"
}

stop_server() {
	local pid
	if pid="$(running_pid)"; then
		kill "${pid}"
		for _ in $(seq 50); do
			kill -0 "${pid}" 2>/dev/null || break
			sleep 0.1
		done
	fi
	rm -f "${PID_FILE}"
}

start_server() {
	(
		cd "${PROD_DIR}/current"
		TICTACTOE_SECRET="$(cat "${SECRET_FILE}")" setsid nohup python3 -m tictactoe --host 127.0.0.1 --port "${PROD_PORT}" \
			>>"${PROD_DIR}/server.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
		echo $! >"${PID_FILE}"
	)
}

smoke_test() {
	local health
	for _ in $(seq 50); do
		health="$(curl -fsS --max-time 1 "${URL}/health" 2>/dev/null)" && break
		sleep 0.1
	done
	[[ "${health:-}" == ok ]] || return 1
	curl -fsS --max-time 2 "${URL}/" | grep -qi '<html'
}

case "${1:-}" in
--status)
	if pid="$(running_pid)"; then
		echo "running: release $(basename "$(readlink "${PROD_DIR}/current")"), pid ${pid}, ${URL}"
	else
		echo "not running"
	fi
	exit 0
	;;
--stop)
	stop_server
	echo "stopped"
	exit 0
	;;
"") ;;
*) fail "unknown option: $1" ;;
esac

cd "${REPO}"

step "Gate 1/4: tests"
python3 -m pytest -q || fail "tests failed"

step "Gate 2/4: ruff check"
ruff check . || fail "lint findings"

step "Gate 3/4: ruff format --check"
ruff format --check . || fail "formatting"

step "Gate 4/4: reviews"
for change in changes/*/; do
	[[ -d "${change}" ]] || continue
	[[ -f "${change}review.md" ]] || fail "${change} has no review.md: it has not been reviewed"
	if grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*- \[ \] \*\*(blocker|major)\*\*' "${change}review.md"; then
		fail "unresolved blocker/major findings in ${change}review.md (above)"
	fi
	echo "${change}: no open blocker or major findings"
done

step "Release"
if [[ ! -f "${SECRET_FILE}" ]]; then
	mkdir -p "${PROD_DIR}"
	(umask 077 && python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))' >"${SECRET_FILE}")
	echo "created the production secret"
fi
id="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
release="${PROD_DIR}/releases/${id}"
[[ -e "${release}" ]] && fail "release ${id} already exists, try again in a second"
mkdir -p "${release}"
cp -r tictactoe "${release}/"
find "${release}" -name __pycache__ -prune -exec rm -rf {} +
commit="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
[[ -n "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ]] && commit+="-dirty"

# Code review: `cheat-code`

Phase 7 of `docs/process.md`. Read: `intent.md`, `spec.md`, `plan.md`,
`preview.md`, `test-report.md`, the diff `git diff e174aff HEAD` (the commit
before the spec), and the code around it (`tictactoe/`, `tests/`,
`docs/architecture.md`, `ops/deploy.sh`). At review time, `python3 -m pytest -q`
gave 215 passed, and `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` were clean.
No code was changed.

**Blocker:** none. **Major:** none.

- [ ] **minor** `tictactoe/server.py:49`: a `game` token is verified and used in `friend` mode too. If you send a computer-game `1.` token with `mode: "friend"`, the friend move uses the after-steal turn rule and the answer says `steal_used: true`. The spec says (lines 182–183) that a friend game answers `steal_used: false`, and `docs/architecture.md` says `level` is "used only against the computer". It can't be exploited: friend mode never issues a token and never allows a steal. But the API breaks its own documented contract, and no test pins this either way. Either refuse or ignore `game` in friend mode, or fix the spec and the architecture doc to describe what happens now.
- [ ] **minor** `tictactoe/static/app.js:151`: when a game ends without a steal (the computer wins, or a draw), the panel still says "No O to steal yet" while Os are on the board. The text is also the steal button's `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader gives the player the wrong reason. The spec defines only two reasons ("No O to steal yet" and "Steal used") and doesn't cover a finished game. Something like "Game over" would be correct.
- [ ] **minor** `docs/architecture.md:3`: the doc no longer describes the whole system. The diagram doesn't show `signing.py`. The "Tests" section (line 173) lists neither `tests/test_signing.py` nor `tests/system/test_cheat.py` and `tests/system/client.py`. `CLAUDE.md` requires a change that adds a module to update this doc.
- [ ] **minor** `changes/cheat-code/spec.md:332`: the intent's success check ("steals in games we did not set up") depends on the client addresses in the request lines. The `steal …` log line itself has no address. But `ops/deploy.sh` starts production on `127.0.0.1`, so outside traffic must come through something local. If that is a reverse proxy, every request line shows `127.0.0.1`, and Product can't tell outside steals from the team's own. Before relying on this measure, ask the platform team whether the real client address reaches the log.
- [ ] **minor** `changes/cheat-code/test-report.md:5`: the report says the page "was checked by a person in `preview.md`". `preview.md` says the opposite: "Checked by: nobody", "Result: not checked". A reader who trusts the test report would believe the browser behaviour was signed off.

## Verdict

The server side is sound and matches the spec. Every steal is judged on
the server. The HMAC game token binds the board, the level and the steal
count, is compared with `compare_digest`, and is handed out only on a chain
that starts from an empty board, so a second steal, a forged or edited
token, a hand-made board and friend-mode steals are all refused. The key is
never logged or sent. Requests without `game` and `steal` go through exactly
the old code path, Hard is unchanged for `steals=0`, and the unit and system
tests cover every rule, error and "must not change" promise in the spec
(including a 2318-request comparison with the baseline server). The page
works out no rule. None of the findings blocks a release.

Whoever releases must weigh one thing: **nobody has looked at the page.**
`preview.md` records an unattended run, "Checked by: nobody", "Result: not
checked", and the test report wrongly claims otherwise. So none of the
browser behaviour has been seen by a person: that the page is unchanged
before the code is typed, how the code is recognised, steal mode with mouse
and keyboard, the screen-reader announcements, the "With help" column, and
the 320 px layout. The 320 px fit depends on the CSS `:has()` selector, which
older browsers ignore. These parts of the intent's "must not change" promise
("the game behaves exactly as it does today", "nobody can steal without typing
the code" on the page) rest only on reading `app.js`.
